shared_elements: low-relief carving on a rectangular stone pillar
long sinuous snake-like form descending the surface
justification: Both show shallow, rounded low relief on a weathered pale limestone pillar in an excavation, and both stack their motifs in vertical registers with a profile animal above a long sinuous snake-like element running downward. The clearest difference is that B carries an elaborate upper frieze of repeated arc-and-disc motifs over a zigzag/net band across a broad face, whereas A's narrow shaft carries a single sparse animal group with no repeated ornamental band.
